newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: London robustas seen up, focus on Brazil - trade.
newsitem.headline: London robustas seen up, focus on Brazil - trade.

text.p: London robusta futures are seen opening US$20-$100 a tonne up later on Tuesday, but the Asian coffee trade remains quiet as the industry keeps close watch on weather forecasts for Brazil, regional dealers said.
Traders said the call on the London market is anywhere from $40-$100 up, but the balance of opinion is towards a $20 rise.
"It should be up by just $20, but the weather will dictate how the market goes," a dealer said.
"It's strictly a weather market," another trader said, adding the gyrations of New York arabicas had made it a "crazy market to follow."
July arabicas climbed 16.05 cents to end on Monday at 253.30 U.S. cents a lb after spending the day bouncing between 235.50 and 256.00 cents.
The July robusta contract in London finished on Monday $67 up on the day at $1,890 a tonne.
"The market moved up on a bit of frost news," one dealer said, adding though that the weather services have been saying there would be no freeze in Brazil, the world's biggest producer of coffee.
"Until the frost season is over, no one wants to be short in this market. Your gains can be limited, but your losses can be unlimited," another dealer said.
The Asian coffee business was quiet, with roasters and exporters sitting on the sidelines waiting for the New York and London markets to calm down.
"In a frost market, the exporters are willing to sit down and wait. The roasters are also not buying anyway," a dealer said.
Indonesian coffee supplies remained steady while Vietnamese exporters are holding back on expectations that prices may still inch higher.
Dealers estimate the Vietnamese still have about 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes of robusta beans left from a harvest that reached between 250,000-270,000 tonnes.
"The quality of the remaining beans is still o.k. They may look small, but above the grade," a trader said.
